allowed_dependency_manifest.content: Fix an integer n greater than 1 and define f(x) = floor(n x) minus the sum from k=1 to n of floor(k x) divided by k. The task is to determine the set of real numbers x such that for every real y, f(x) is greater than or equal to f(y), and to compute the corresponding maximum value m equal to f(x).
allowed_dependency_manifest.label: root_semantic_sketch

forbidden_claims.label: root_theorem_claim
forbidden_claims.reason: root theorem proposition is not citable solver context
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.role_in_assembly: Reduces the continuum problem on [0,1) to the discrete grid points j/n.

domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n greater than 1
k ranges over integers from 1 through n inclusive
x ranges over all real numbers
y ranges over all real numbers
floor(t) denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to t
root_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Fix an integer n greater than 1 and define f(x) = floor(n x) minus the sum from k=1 to n of floor(k x) divided by k. The task is to determine the set of real numbers x such that for every real y, f(x) is greater than or equal to f(y), and to compute the corresponding maximum value m equal to f(x).
quantifier_order: for all integers n with n greater than 1
there exists a real number x that maximizes the expression
for all real numbers y, the expression at x is greater than or equal to the expression at y

variables.name: n
variables.role: fixed parameter for the maximization problem

variables.name: y
variables.role: comparison point for defining maximality of x

witness_dependencies: the maximizing x may depend on n
the maximal value m may depend on n

domain_restrictions: n is a positive integer (implicit, needed so that j/n and (j+1)/n are well-defined and intervals make sense)
j is an integer satisfying 0 <= j <= n - 1
x is a real number satisfying j/n <= x < (j+1)/n
F_n is defined at every real x considered, and in particular at x equal to j/n
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every positive integer n, for every integer j with 0 <= j <= n - 1, and for every real number x with j/n <= x and x < (j+1)/n, the inequality F_n(x) <= F_n(j/n) holds.

variables.name: n
variables.role: index parameter for the function F_n and for defining interval endpoints j/n and (j+1)/n

variables.name: j
variables.role: cell index that selects the interval [j/n, (j+1)/n)

variables.name: x
variables.role: argument of the function F_n within the interval associated to j

witness_dependencies: none (the claim is universally quantified; no existential witnesses are introduced)

payload.statement_nl: For any integer j with 0 <= j <= n - 1 and any real number x with j/n <= x < (j+1)/n, one has F_n(x) <= F_n(j/n).
